input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate: Talk with RAINN, a therapist, or counsel before deciding whether to report. Keep the phone channel open unless a concrete tripwire fires: a request to meet, sexual images, threats, evidence of other minors, migration to hidden channels, or your daughter saying she feels pressured or afraid.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Use a safety-first plan with professional support. Keep trust central, monitor for concerning signals, preserve communication boundaries, and escalate if the situation becomes more dangerous. Do not treat quiet behavior as proof that risk has disappeared.

step6_output.answer_core: You can keep the situation grounded by getting guidance from RAINN, a therapist, or legal counsel before deciding what to do next. Stay in open communication with your daughter and keep an eye on specific tripwires: requests to meet, sexual images, threats, signs of other minors being involved, a shift to hidden channels, or her saying she feels pressured or afraid. As long as none of those appear, focus on maintaining trust, clear boundaries, and access to professional support. If any tripwire shows up or the situation feels more dangerous, escalate with professional help right away.
